claims.text: Toughness is retained when a controlled dual-phase microstructure fosters localized transformation-induced plasticity at crack tips.
A small Nb addition promotes nanoscale precipitates or segregations.
Nb-induced precipitates or segregations act as nucleation sites for a metastable phase transformation during deformation.
A deformation-induced metastable phase transformation blunts cracks and dissipates energy.
The initial homogenized, as-cast alloy is primarily a disordered solid solution.
Adding 1–2 at.% of a minor element such as Nb can promote nanoprecipitate formation.
A tailored heat treatment can promote nanoprecipitate formation.
Transformation-induced plasticity can occur at moderate temperatures and strain rates representative of engineering applications.
Nanometer-scale precipitates or local compositional fluctuations at grain boundaries enable formation of a metastable phase during deformation.
The added element induces local heterogeneities that trigger transformation-induced plasticity under stress.
Transformation of a metastable phase at crack tips absorbs energy and blunts the crack.
Crack-tip transformation-induced plasticity retains overall toughness.
The Nb-modified alloy should have greater fracture toughness than the baseline alloy.
Localized phase transformations should be observable near crack-initiation sites in the modified alloy.
The baseline alloy loses toughness more rapidly under comparable loading than the modified alloy.
The baseline alloy's more rapid toughness loss is caused by a lack of localized transformation-induced plasticity.
The proposed mechanism is expected to govern toughness only over a moderate-temperature, moderate-strain-rate operating range.
At very low temperatures or extremely high strain rates, mechanisms other than the proposed transformation-induced plasticity mechanism may dominate toughness.
